SABIC Unveils Major Expansion Plan for Petrochemical Complex in Jubail

Saudi Basic Industries Corp has announced a significant investment in expanding its petrochemical manufacturing capacity in Jubail Industrial City, reaffirming the company’s commitment to supporting Saudi Arabia’s economic diversification goals.

The new project, valued at around $1.2 billion, will see the construction of additional production facilities aimed at increasing output of key chemicals, including ethylene and polyethylene. The expansion is expected to boost Saudi Basic Industries Corp’s annual production capacity by nearly 10%, catering to both domestic and international demand.

In a statement, CEO Khalid Al-Mutlaq said, “This expansion underscores our dedication to advancing the Kingdom’s Vision 2030 by strengthening our industrial base and enhancing export capabilities. The new facilities will leverage the latest process technologies to ensure world-class efficiency and sustainability.”

Industry observers view the move as a strategic response to growing demand for advanced materials in sectors such as packaging, construction, and automotive manufacturing. “The chemicals sector in Saudi Arabia is expected to maintain robust growth thanks to continued investments from major players like Saudi Basic Industries Corp,” commented Sara Al-Jaber, a Riyadh-based chemicals industry analyst. “Such expansions will further consolidate the Kingdom’s position as a global hub for petrochemicals.”

The expansion is projected to create approximately 750 direct jobs and an additional 2,000 indirect employment opportunities during the construction phase. Dr. Fahad Al-Osaimi, president of the Saudi Chemical Producers Association, welcomed the development, noting, “This initiative will contribute significantly to local content and knowledge transfer, supporting the broader goals of industrialization.”

Construction is scheduled to begin in Q4 2024, with commercial operations expected by early 2027. The announcement comes amid ongoing efforts across the region to attract foreign investment and develop downstream industries linked to the chemicals value chain.
